structured.approach: The only input is a one-paragraph calendar rules file. I restated its facts in a structured layout and did not invent the iteration or release train dates it lacks. I listed those gaps as non-blocking open questions for the RTE. I didn't use connectors or the verifier, because the output is a few facts taken straight from the input.

claims.text: The system demo was held on 24 October 2026 at 15:00.
The PROD window is 11:00-12:00 on the day after the system demo, which is 25 October 2026.
The timezone is Asia/Kolkata and there are no holidays in the window.
The step is for ITER-2026-10, with a trigger calendar date of 2026-10-25.

The workbook action asks for iteration dates, release train dates, the PROD window (11 am–12 pm, day after system demo), timezone and holidays, but the input holds no iteration or release train dates.

open_questions: Non-blocking: What are the ITER-2026-10 start and end dates? The input does not give them, so the output leaves them unrecorded.
Non-blocking: What are the release train dates? The input does not give them, so the output leaves them unrecorded.
Non-blocking: Is 25 October 2026 correct for a PROD window? By my own calendar reckoning it is a Sunday, and the input says nothing about weekends or working days. RTE to confirm.
structured.summary: I wrote org/org.calendar_rules.md with the system demo (24 Oct 2026, 15:00), the PROD window (11:00-12:00 on 25 Oct 2026), the timezone (Asia/Kolkata) and no holidays. Iteration dates and release train dates are not in the input, so I left them blank and raised them as non-blocking questions for the RTE. I also asked the RTE to confirm that 25 Oct 2026 works as a PROD day, since it appears to fall on a Sunday.
